entities.name: PMID:25445161
observations: 2015 Digestive Diseases and Sciences primary in-vitro study titled “Bone Marrow Stromal Cells Inhibit the Activation of Liver Cirrhotic Fat-Storing Cells via Adrenomedullin Secretion.”
Used rat bone-marrow stromal-cell supernatant with cultured rat cirrhotic fat-storing cells, equivalent to hepatic stellate cells.
Reported adrenomedullin supplementation and adrenomedullin-specific siRNA experiments; detailed quantitative outcomes were not available in the abstract.

entities.name: Bone marrow stromal cells
observations: Rat bone-marrow stromal-cell supernatant inhibited cultured cirrhotic fat-storing-cell proliferation and activation in vitro.

entities.name: Adrenomedullin
observations: BMSC-secreted adrenomedullin was implicated as the mediator of reduced cirrhotic fat-storing-cell activation.
Recombinant rat adrenomedullin supplementation and adrenomedullin-specific siRNA knockdown were used as gain- and loss-of-function interventions.

entities.name: Cirrhotic fat-storing cells
observations: Rat cirrhotic fat-storing cells, a hepatic stellate-cell model, showed reduced proliferation and activation after exposure to BMSC supernatant in vitro.
Reported downstream reductions included angiotensin II, AT1 receptor, and p47-phox signaling.

entities.name: BMSC-AM anti-activation
observations: In a rat in-vitro model, BMSC-conditioned medium inhibited cirrhotic hepatic stellate-cell proliferation and activation, with adrenomedullin implicated by supplementation and siRNA experiments.
The accessible evidence does not provide numerical effect sizes, dose-response data, or enough detail to quantify adrenomedullin necessity or sufficiency.
Focused searching found no additional primary study directly testing this specific BMSC–adrenomedullin–cirrhotic hepatic stellate-cell claim.
